## Problem 1

(1 point)
Which of the following values of $R^2$ indicates the best fit to the data?
Select only one.

(a) $0.34$
(b) $0.43$
(c) $0.58$
(d) $0.60$


::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

D

:::

## Problem 2

(4 points)
Which of the following metrics is/are intended to prevent overfitting?
Select all that apply.


(a) $R^2$
(b) $R_\text{adj}^2$
(c) Likelihood
(d) AIC


::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

B and D

:::

## Problem 3

Suppose you have three multiple regression models that differ only in what explanatory variables
they include. The three models are:

- Model 1: $E(Y_i|A_i,B_i,C_i,D_i) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 A_i + \beta_2 B_i + \beta_3 C_i + \beta_4 D_i$;
- Model 2: $E(Y_i|A_i,B_i,C_i) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 A_i + \beta_2 B_i + \beta_3 C_i$; and
- Model 3: $E(Y_i|A_i,B_i) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 A_i + \beta_2 B_i$.

Please answer the following questions based on these three models.
Assume all four of our assumptions are met for each model.



### Part (a)

(4 points)
Which of the following statements is/are true?
Select all that apply.


(i) Model 3 is nested within Model 2.
(ii) Model 3 is nested within Model 1.
(iii) Model 2 is nested within Model 3.
(iv) Model 2 is nested within Model 1.


::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

i, ii, and iv

:::

### Part (b)

(4 points)
Suppose $D_3$ is missing in the data set, i.e., the third participant
is missing a value for the fourth explanatory variable.
There is no other missing data in the data set.
Which of the following metrics could you use to compare Model 1 and Model 2?
Select all that apply.


(i) $R^2$
(ii) $R_\text{adj}^2$
(iii) Likelihood
(iv) AIC


::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

i and ii

:::

### Part (c)

(4 points)
Suppose $D_3$ is missing in the data set, i.e., the third participant
is missing a value for the fourth explanatory variable.
There is no other missing data in the data set.
Which of the following metrics could you use to compare Model 2 and Model 3?
Select all that apply.


(i) $R^2$
(ii) $R_\text{adj}^2$
(iii) Likelihood
(iv) AIC


::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

i, ii, iii, and iv

:::

### Part (d)

(4 points)
Suppose $A_3$ is missing in the data set, i.e., the third participant
is missing a value for the first explanatory variable.
There is no other missing data in the data set.
Which of the following metrics could you use to compare Model 2 and Model 3?
Select all that apply.


(i) $R^2$
(ii) $R_\text{adj}^2$
(iii) Likelihood
(iv) AIC


::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

i, ii, iii, and iv

:::

### Part (e)

(4 points)
Suppose you use a likelihood ratio test to compare Model 1 to Model 3.
You obtain a p-value of 0.00001.
What is a reasonable conclusion from this result?
Select all that apply.


(i) Model 3 is at least as good as Model 1.
(ii) Model 3 fits the data better than Model 1.
(iii) Model 2 is at least as good as Model 3.
(iv) Model 1 fits the data better than Model 3.


::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

iv

:::

## Problem 4

Please identify each of the following statements as true or false.
Each problem is worth one point.
You do not need to justify your answers.

### Part (a)

Adding more explanatory variables to the model increases the risk of overfitting.

::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

True

:::

### Part (b)

Maximizing the $R^2$ maximizes our ability to generalize to new data.

::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

False

:::

### Part (c)

        The AIC and likelihood ratio test will always agree on the best model.

::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

False

:::

### Part (d)

Testing a model on new data can help us determine if it has been overfit.

::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

True

:::

### Part (e)

A high AIC is better than a low AIC.

::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

False

:::

### Part (f)

It is appropriate to use the $R^2$ for model selection when only some of the
assumptions of linear regression are met.

::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

True

:::

### Part (g)

It is appropriate to use the $R^2_\text{adj}$ for model selection when only some of the
assumptions of linear regression are met.

::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

True

:::

### Part (h)

The likelihood ratio test cannot be used to compare nested models.

::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

False

:::

### Part (i)

The AIC cannot be used to compare nested models.

::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

False

:::
